extracted.intended_audience: media, NBA fans, team/league communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Short biographical roster entries for NBA referees used in a media/press guide or press release, combining career statistics, background, and light personal/fun-fact items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name and number header
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee's full name followed by their jersey/ID number (e.g., 'TRE MADDOX #23').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed prominently at top of entry as a header; often in uppercase. Use consistent formatting across entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA Experience
rubrics_metrics.description: A short line stating the referee's NBA tenure (e.g., 'NBA Experience: 10th season', '1st season').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State current season count (ordinal) and/or number of seasons on staff; place near the top so reader immediately knows experience level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Birth information
rubrics_metrics.description: Birth date and birthplace line (e.g., 'Born: October 7, 1967 (Great Lakes, Ill.)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full birth date and city/state/country in parentheses; useful for age and origin context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence
rubrics_metrics.description: Current hometown or residence (e.g., 'Resides: Las Vegas, Nev.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short city/state line indicating where the official lives when not on assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: High School
rubrics_metrics.description: Line naming the high school attended (e.g., 'High School: Wyandotte (Kansas City, Kan.)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include school name and location; helpful for local-interest connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: College
rubrics_metrics.description: College/university attended and sometimes graduation year or degree (e.g., 'College: Dakota State University', 'Thomas Jefferson University ’93').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List institution and, when available, graduation year or degree to establish educational background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officiating career summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative paragraph summarizing NBA games officiated, playoff appearances, debut seasons, and other high-level career milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include total regular-season and playoff game counts, year of playoff debut, notable firsts, and concise timeline of NBA service. Example phrasing: 'has officiated 495 regular-season games and 10 playoff games in nine seasons.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Game and assignment statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit counts of games officiated (regular-season, playoff) and mention of All-Star/Finals assignments when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric tallies (e.g., '1,981 regular-season games', '218 playoff games') and flag special assignments (All-Star Game, Finals) as notable achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior officiating leagues and levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing of prior officiating experience in other leagues and levels (e.g., NBA G League, WNBA, CBA, collegiate conferences, high school).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State seasons/years or notable assignments in each prior league; specify collegiate conferences (ACC, Pac-12, Big Ten, etc.) to demonstrate breadth of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable assignments / highlights
rubrics_metrics.description: A short mention of especially memorable games or moments (e.g., 'first game: a double-overtime matchup between the LA Clippers and the Utah Jazz').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a one-sentence anecdote highlighting a standout game or milestone to humanize the profile and show career highlights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and academic degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Details on degrees, majors, and institutions (e.g., 'received a bachelor’s degree in Elementary Education', 'earned a bachelor’s degree in Marketing').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include major/degree and honors when available to provide fuller biographical context beyond officiating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community involvement and charitable work
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of camps, foundations, volunteer work, or fundraising efforts the official supports (e.g., directing a camp that benefits under-privileged youth, supporting Salvation Army).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight organizations, programs, and missions; describe roles (director, contributor, volunteer) and beneficiaries to illustrate off-court impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal life and hobbies
rubrics_metrics.description: Short notes about family status, hobbies, and interests (e.g., 'married with three children', 'enjoys reading, working out, bicycling and yoga').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep brief, relatable details that give personality—family, leisure activities, and interests that are non-professional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior non-officiating careers
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention of significant prior jobs outside officiating (e.g., teacher, real estate agent, police officer, wildland firefighter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include job title, employer or role, and years where relevant; these items show broader life experience and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronunciation guide for name
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical pronunciation key for names with phonetic spelling (e.g., 'Moyer-Gleich (gleash)', 'Petraitis (Geh-di-mihn-us pet-RYE-tis)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short phonetic cue immediately after the name where needed to assist announcers and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: FUN FACTS section with standardized subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: A labeled 'FUN FACTS' block listing light personal items such as Favorite TV Show, Favorite Movie, Favorite Musician, Favorite Book, Favorite Meal, Favorite App, Would Most Like To Visit, Bucket List, Hidden Talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this consistent list of short-answer personal items to add color; use the same subfield labels across entries for readability and quick scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hometown / formative athletic participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on the official's athletic background or local achievements (e.g., played basketball in college/high school, All-Conference honors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention playing history, honors, or local athletic accomplishments to provide connection to the sport and early career.

rubrics_metrics.name: International / citizenship notes
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, mention country of birth, naturalization, or international officiating roles (e.g., 'Born in Lithuania, became a U.S. citizen in 2015', 'served as a FIBA referee').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include international affiliations or citizenship changes and foreign assignments to reflect global experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise formatting and repeatable template
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall entry follows a concise, repeatable template: header (name/#), short metadata lines (NBA Experience, Born, Resides, High School, College), career narrative paragraph(s), 'FUN FACTS' block, and closing personal/community notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent ordering and labels across all entries for uniformity in a media guide; keep prose concise and factual, reserve anecdotes to single sentences.
